transcript: Ranking film adaptations of Macbeth. I got a bunch of requests for this after my Hamlet video, so here you go. Some people were very upset and confused about how I narrowed down the list, so I'm doing it a little differently this time. I'm still excluding pro-shots, but I am including the made for TV Versions and the loose reimaginings *that I have seen* I have not seen every version of Macbeth caught on camera. You’re welcome to make your own video with the rest. It's really not that serious. Easily in last place is the 2015 version with Michael Fassbender. They had the nerve to take one of Shakespeare's most tightly paced, already very cinematic plays and turn it into just a sluggish, inert mess. It's beautiful to look at, don't get me wrong, but it's terribly paced. There's no sense of tension. The actors are like muttering unintelligibly under their breath. So many unforced errors in this interminable slog of a movie. Next, the 1971 version directed by R***n P******i This one's serviceable, I guess. It's kind of a nasty and strange at times, in a way that I guess makes sense for Macbeth, but maybe isn't always for me. But mainly also just f**k R***n P******i Next I have Scotland PA. Which is a reimagining set in a burger joint. It's got a very indie vibe. Kind of rough around the edges. Not the greatest movie ever made, but I don't know, it's a fun watch. Next up the Orson Welles film, which is in many ways just a very classic old school film adaptation of Shakespeare. But of course, Orson Welles’ style is a great fit for this material. I think it's a solid adaptation. Next up, the made for TV Version starring Patrick Stewart, directed by Rupert Goold, based on his stage production. This one's wild. It has like a mid 20th century Eastern European feel. Some of it feels like it's in a bunker with these, like, fluorescent lit corridors. The witches are like hospital nurses. I've always liked the vibe and the energy of this one. I think Patrick Stewart is a great Macbeth. It is maybe a little overlong, but otherwise I like it. I have Kurasawa's Throne of Blood in second place. I know a lot of people are gonna be mad at me for that, but again, make your own video. This is obviously one of the great Shakespeare reimaginings, though, from a legendary filmmaker. I have nothing against it. I just really like the Joel Coen version. This is the one with Denzel Washington and Frances Mcdormand and the great Kathryn Hunter as the witch. I think Coen really has the best of both worlds here, where it's in many ways a very straightforward, traditional take on the play. But they make some smart cuts and smart changes. Like, I love what they do with the character of Ross, and it has this cool aesthetic that is kind Of an homage to Orson Welles and German Expressionism. That gives the movie kind of a self aware quality, even like a little edge of dark humor underneath it. And maybe most importantly, same with my Hamlet video. If I'm in the mood to watch a version of Macbeth on screen, this is probably the one I'm gonna pull up first. And that's why I put it number one.
